events.title: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel
events.narrative_summary: God tells Jacob to arise, go up to Bethel, dwell there and make an altar to the God who appeared to him when he fled from Esau.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word. Anchored on the end of the rebuke in Gen 34:30-31, with a 1-day offset and a 2-day margin, since the text just continues the story after Shechem. DAY_SEQUENCE like the chapter 34 events.

events.title: Jacob has his household give up foreign gods
events.narrative_summary: Jacob orders his household to put away foreign gods, purify themselves and change clothes. They hand over their idols and earrings and Jacob buries them under the oak at Shechem.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the command with no delay (35:2 'Then Jacob said'). Gathering and burying take a few hours, 4 hours, with a margin of 6 hours.

events.title: Jacob's company travels to Bethel unpursued
events.narrative_summary: They set out, and the terror of God keeps the surrounding cities from pursuing them. Jacob and all his people come to Luz, which is Bethel.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: urim travel Shechem to Bethel: 33 km straight, about 41 km by road, donkey 4 km/h, 10.2 h moving, about 1 day. A company with flocks and children would take about one day, so duration 1 day, margin 6 hours.

events.title: Jacob builds an altar at Bethel and names the place
events.narrative_summary: Jacob builds an altar at Bethel and calls the place El-Bethel, because God revealed himself to him there when he fled from his brother.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows arrival (35:7), the command of 35:1 and the vow of 35:3 carried out. A few hours after arrival; margin 1 day for setting up camp.

events.title: Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, dies and is buried under an oak
events.narrative_summary: Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, dies and is buried below Bethel under an oak, which is called Allon-bacuth.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word. Placed by verse order after the altar, 3 days later with a 3-day margin. DAY_SEQUENCE like the other Bethel events, which this scene falls among; the 3-day offset and margin are estimates. Burial takes 1 day.

events.title: God appears to Jacob again and renames him Israel
events.narrative_summary: God appears again to Jacob as he comes from Paddan-aram, blesses him, and says his name will no longer be Jacob but Israel.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Again' (35:9) ties it to the visit at Bethel; no time word. Anchored 1 day after Deborah's burial with a 2-day margin, by verse order.

events.title: God promises Jacob nations, kings and the land
events.narrative_summary: God, speaking as God Almighty, tells Jacob to be fruitful, promises a nation and a company of nations, kings from his loins, and the land given to Abraham and Isaac; then God goes up from him.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: A continuation of the same speech (35:11 'And God said to him'): starts when the renaming ends. 30 minutes.

events.title: Jacob sets up a stone pillar and pours offerings on it
events.narrative_summary: Jacob sets up a stone pillar where God spoke with him, pours out a drink offering and oil on it, and names the place Bethel.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows God's departure at once (35:13-14); about 2 hours.

events.title: Rachel goes into hard labour near Ephrath
events.narrative_summary: They leave Bethel, and a short way before Ephrath Rachel goes into hard labour; the midwife tells her not to fear, for she has another son.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: They 'journeyed from Bethel' with no stated delay. urim travel Bethel to Bethlehem: 25 km straight, 31 km by road, donkey about 7.5 hours; the labour is 'a little way' short of Ephrath. Offset 30 hours after the pillar (some time at Bethel plus about 6 hours on the road), margin 2 days.

events.title: Rachel dies bearing Benjamin and is buried
events.narrative_summary: As her life departs Rachel names her son Ben-oni, but Jacob calls him Benjamin. Rachel dies and is buried on the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: She dies in the same labour (35:18), so the event follows the labour's end directly. The burial is the same day, 1 day in all.

events.title: Jacob sets up a pillar over Rachel's grave
events.narrative_summary: Jacob sets up a pillar over Rachel's grave, which is still its marker 'to this day'.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word; a day after the burial for the work, 2-day margin.

events.title: Israel moves on and pitches his tent beyond Migdal-eder
events.narrative_summary: Israel travels on and pitches his tent beyond the tower of Eder.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Bethlehem to the tower of Eder is about 2 km straight, so it takes under an hour. Offset 1 day after the pillar, margin 2 days for mourning; no time word.

events.title: Reuben lies with Bilhah and Israel hears of it
events.narrative_summary: While Israel dwells in that land, Reuben goes and lies with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and Israel hears of it.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'When Israel dwelt in that land' gives no interval. I estimate 2 months after Eder, margin 2 months. MACRO_ERA because the text gives no time.

events.title: Jacob comes to his father Isaac at Mamre
events.narrative_summary: Jacob comes to his father Isaac at Mamre, Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac lived as sojourners.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No interval stated. 6 months after the previous scene, with a 6-month margin. The journey Eder to Hebron is about 24 km straight, a day by donkey. Must be before Joseph is 17 (Gen 37:14).

events.title: Isaac dies at 180 and Esau and Jacob bury him
events.narrative_summary: Isaac lives 180 years, dies old and full of days, and is gathered to his people. Esau and Jacob, his sons, bury him.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Age 180 (35:28): offset 180 years from anchor.isaac_birth, margin 1 year since an age covers the whole year. About 1886 BCE. Burial takes about a day. Told here out of time order (see Ramban on 35:28).
events.ancient_year_marker: The days of Isaac were a hundred and eighty years

causal_edges.causal_explanation: Jacob does what God commanded in 35:1 and builds the altar at Bethel (35:7).
Jacob prepares his household for the trip to Bethel that God ordered, purging idols first (35:1-2).
Jacob marks Rachel's burial place with a pillar after she dies (35:19-20).
Rachel's hard labour ends in her death as she bears Benjamin (35:16-18).
